Hi Jacob —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then a worked example and links. Happy to run through this on a call; proposing Thu 12/10 10am PT if that works for your team.

High-level metering rules (hosted API):
- We charge for two buckets per model invocation: "prompt/input tokens" and "response/output tokens."
- System messages are included in the prompt/input bucket. Any token that is part of the request payload (user, system, or assistant context you send) counts as input.
- Tool/function calls: tokens produced by the model as part of the generation (including function call tokens if the model emits the call) are billed as output. If an external tool returns content that we then include back into the model prompt (e.g., tool result re-submitted), that returned text will count as input on the subsequent request.
- Streaming: billing is applied to the final token counts for the request. We do not bill per-chunk. If a stream is terminated early, billing reflects the tokens actually generated.
- Rounding: we meter tokens as integer token counts per-request (tokenizers produce integer token counts). We do not charge fractional tokens; counts are exact integers from the tokenizer. Aggregation and invoices sum those integers; there is no per-token microbilling below tokenizer granularity.
- Caching/deduplication: we offer optional prefix/KV caching for customer workloads (configurable). Cached responses still appear as model output on first generation; subsequent identical cache hits are served from the cache and do not re-execute model generation (so they produce no additional model output tokens). If your architecture stores tool outputs and re-injects them into prompts, you'll see them as input tokens on the request where they're included.

Worked example (your numbers):
- Request payload: system 20 + user 50 = 70 input tokens.
- Model generates a function call and 200 tokens of normal text; model-generated function call tokens and the 200 tokens are billed as output (so output = 200 + any function-call tokens emitted by the model; for this example assume function-call framing is 0 extra tokens).
- External tool returns 150 tokens and you do NOT re-submit that text to the model: those 150 tokens are not billed by Redwood (tools executed outside the model do not incur model output tokens unless the model itself generated them).
- If, however, you include the 150-token tool response back into the model as the next prompt, those 150 tokens will be counted as input on that subsequent request.

Cost math (example using list rates):
- List rate: $0.004 / 1K input tokens, $0.020 / 1K output tokens (example tier; see attached ratecard for model-specific rates).
- Monthly volume (sample): 1.2M calls * (70 input + 200 output) = 1.2M * 270 tokens = 324M tokens (broken down: 84M input, 240M output).
- Cost: (84M / 1000) * $0.004 = $336; (240M / 1000) * $0.020 = $4,800 → total list = $5,136/month.

Discounts: we offer volume/commitment tiers and multi-year credits. For pipeline-level discussions I can share targeted discount ranges; for ACME Health we typically start commercial talks at a committed spend threshold (e.g., $100k ARR) and scale discounts with commitment and length. I'll loop in Ben for commercial specifics.
